  (C) What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?

RELEVANT = the text describes the writer's own (or other investors') SIP experience, motives, expectations, behaviour or decisions that speak to A, B or C - including payment/mandate/app problems that make a SIP miss or stop.
NOT RELEVANT = generic praise or complaints about the app, stock trading only, SIPs merely named with nothing about motives/expectations/behaviour/decisions, spam or promotion, thanks to a video creator, or bare how-to questions with no personal situation.
The context line (video or forum topic title) is background only; judge the text.

Return a JSON array with one object per item: [{"i": <item number>, "relevant": true|false}]

[8] (source: tradingqna; context: About MF Regular plan)
When Direct plans were first introduced I had followed this approach:
 Stop my SIPs in the regular plans.
 Start the same SIPs in the Direct Funds
 STP from Regular Plan to Direct Plan keeping the Exit Loads & LTGC in mind. That is, if I had a SIP active till last month, I create a STP such that the last STP transactions happens 12 months after the last SIP in the regular Plan so that I cross the 1 year period - both for Exit Load and LTGC - for each SIP transactions.
 This last point is important - each SIP is actually a “Purchase” in the MF and will incur Exit Load and LTGC rules accordingly. I designed a “rolling pull out” so that each SIP date was taken care of. By this means I managed not t pay any Exit Load or STGC for my investments in the Regular Plans.
 Also, the agent cannot deduct anything from your account. You don’t have to depend on them at all. Just use the Folio Number to start a STP or redemption as the case might be. This can be done directly on the AMC’s web site after eKYC and account creation. And you don’t need the agent’s permission to make changes to your investments - they are your and you have total control over them. The agent does not.
